newsitem.title: USA: Strip club tax proposed in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Strip club tax proposed in Florida.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles has proposed a ticket tax at clubs that offer lap dances, peep shows and other live adult entertainment, according to budget aides and published reports Monday.
"It's a sales tax on the admission, not on the services performed," one of the governor's budget aides told Reuters.

The proposal is part of a $41 billion budget plan for fiscal 1998 that Chiles will formally unveil Wednesday. The levy, which would also apply to massage parlours, peep shows, escort services and topless clubs, would raise $9 million a year when fully implemented.
Opponents said taxing such forms of entertainment would be tantamount to granting a state seal of approval.
"Why would you want to legitimise something by taxing it?" Florida House Speaker Dan Webster, R-Orlando, asked. "I'd stay away from this idea," he told Fort Lauderdale's Sun-Sentinel.
But the budget official said the issue was equalisation of tax treatment. "Florida already taxes other admissions -- movie theatres, concert tickets," he said.

"Why should adult entertainment establishments escape the tax when a lot of other places that compete with them are paying it? It's a small way to make the sales tax on admissions a little bit fairer."
